<issue>
A -P proxy given as a bracketed IPv6 literal with no port parses to a truncated host and port 1
`hts_parse_proxy` scans backward from the end of the `-P` argument looking for the port colon, stopping at the authority start or a userinfo `@`. Nothing stops it at a `]`, so for a bracketed IPv6 literal with no explicit port the scan walks into the literal and stops at one of the literal's own colons.

`httrack -#test=proxyurl 'http://[2001:db8::1]'` prints:

```
name=http://[2001:db8: port=1 host=[2001:db8: kind=http
```

The name is truncated mid-literal and the port becomes 1, from `sscanf("1]", "%d")`. Same for `socks5://[::1]` and for the bare `[::1]` form. An explicit port (`[::1]:3128`) is unaffected, which is why the usual form works.

The bug is long-standing. The pre-#566 inline parser in `htscoremain.c` used the same backward scan with no bracket guard; #566 moved it into `hts_parse_proxy` and kept the shape. It affects `http://`, `connect://` and `socks5://` proxies equally.


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.
